- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a spike in price, model often overshoots and fails to correct downward — overreacts to recent volatility.
- Model underestimates the mean reversion tendency — fails to recognize that prices often return to prior levels after sharp moves.
- Forecast bias is stronger in the second half of the 30-day window — model consistently underestimates later periods.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — delays correction, leading to persistent underestimation.
- When history shows strong upward momentum, model fails to anticipate further gains — underestimates continuation of trend.
- Model overfits to recent high prices — fails to account for seasonal or policy-driven downward pressure.
- Model is sensitive to early data points — overweights recent values, leading to overestimation of short-term volatility.
